title: Axiomatization of the Levin--Wen Wave Function
abstract: The Levin--Wen model provides a lattice realization of topological orders associated with a given unitary fusion category. A longstanding open problem is to characterize Levin--Wen ground-state wave functions intrinsically, without assuming a priori categorical symmetry data or a Hamiltonian. We address this by proposing six axioms on a family of wave functions defined on lattices at multiple scales. These axioms allow us to reconstruct the underlying unitary fusion category and prove that the resulting wave functions map to nonzero Levin--Wen ground-state vectors of the emergent category.
summary: This paper introduces a set of six mathematical axioms designed to characterize the ground-state wave functions of the Levin--Wen model intrinsically. By imposing these axioms on multi-scale wave functions, the authors successfully reconstruct the underlying unitary fusion category and prove that the resulting state is a valid topological ground state. This offers a powerful, axiomatic framework for understanding topological order beyond Hamiltonian assumptions.
main_problem: The central problem is to characterize the ground-state wave functions of the Levin--Wen model intrinsically, without relying on prior knowledge of the underlying Hamiltonian or categorical symmetry data.
main_result: The authors propose six axioms on multi-scale wave functions that are sufficient to uniquely reconstruct the underlying unitary fusion category and prove the resulting state is a non-zero Levin--Wen ground state.
method: The approach involves developing and applying a set of axioms to a family of wave functions, utilizing specialized mathematical tools like $S_n$-functionals and analyzing the structure of $C^*$-tensor categories.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Levin--Wen model, which realizes topological order associated with a unitary fusion category on a lattice embedded in the 2D sphere. The ground state is defined by the common eigenspace of local edge and plaquette projection operators.
key_observables: The $S_2$-functional, the one-site reduced density matrix $D$, and the emergent unitary fusion category $C$.
important_parameters: Topological parameters $	au$ and $\mu$, and the scale factor $\lambda$ measuring the discrepancy between prescribed and reconstructed inner products.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a multi-scale wave function satisfying the proposed axioms, and later work suggests generalizing the exchange relation to higher dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the Levin--Wen model and its Hamiltonian structure to introducing the $S_2$-functionals. It then systematically develops and verifies the six axioms, culminating in theorems that establish the equivalence between satisfying these axioms and possessing a valid ground state.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, purely axiomatic characterization of topological order states, linking abstract mathematical structures (fusion categories) directly to physical ground states in a way that is highly relevant to understanding entanglement and topological phases in quantum systems.
